caveats: The market is hard to beat. Over the last 3 years the rule's tickets won 126 of 369 (+5% a ticket, -10% to +20%); the market-only control's won 110 of 346 (-3%). An interval that spans zero is no evidence of an edge.
Measured to 2026-08-08, the last day all three sports' leg tables cover (UFC 2026-08-08, NFL 2026-11-08, soccer 2026-11-08); the UFC walk-forward needs a runner refit to go further.

Prices: UFC at each card's closing (or, where only that exists, opening) line, NFL at the closing moneyline, soccer at the pre-match average posted on Friday or Tuesday afternoon. A ticket built earlier in the day gets different prices; NFL closing lines know the day's news.

Payouts: these files' margins are lower than those of the consensus moneylines the NFL app logged live (NFL closing 2.8% a game, the median here, against 4.0% on the 45 games logged live), so a live NFL leg at the same chance pays less than the record assumes: 1.2% a leg, 3.3% on a ticket of the record's 2.87 legs on average were every leg priced so.
Soccer here is the top five leagues only, which play no matches on international-break weekends and in June-July; on those days a ticket comes from UFC and NFL alone, or there is none.
UFC days are the event date; a card held outside the Americas can fall on another ET date.

UFC draws and no contests: 92 of the 5,050 UFC fights from 2016-08-01 to 2026-08-08 (1.8%) ended without a winner - 40 draws, 52 no contests or overturned results, counted from the UFC archive - and none of them is in the history's legs (engine/experiments/parlay_legs.csv.gz keeps decided fights only), so here they are neither legs nor underdogs and a ticket that day is drawn and filled from the other fights. Live the rule cannot know them beforehand: such a fight stays in the draw and the fill, and its leg voids (pays 1.0).
The likeliest ticket in 3-5x is mostly favourites, and every leg is the same model's opinion; the legs are different events, so their outcomes are close to independent.

The market is hard to beat, and a draw cannot create an edge: every 3-5x ticket pays the bookmaker's margin on every leg. This ticket is for variety and a bigger payout, never the better bet. At the live draw it won 397 of 1,487 (-1.6% a ticket, -9.9% to +7.0%; over the 1,000 simulation draws -9.9% (-14.7% to -4.7%), by the prices -8.5%); an interval that spans zero is no evidence of an edge.

Expected before any result was seen (sameday.py): by the prices it lands about 1 time in 4 (a market chance of about 0.25 at about 3.8x), the likeliest about 2 in 7 at about 3.1x, price-implied about -8% a ticket, and somewhat worse than its prices imply. The prices on file give the live draw's tickets a market chance of 0.244 at 3.83x, price-implied -8.5%, and the 1,000 simulation draws' 0.244 at 3.83x, -8.5%.

Prior exposure: the rule's own results were not seen before it was fixed, but underdog results over the same years had been - the UFC profiles' risker and risk-lover tickets and the NFL and soccer edge-betting checks. Its record is not an out-of-sample test of underdogs.

Bookmakers load more margin on underdogs (about 5% on a dog leg against 3% on a favourite, as written before the results), so a dog ticket pays the heavier margin once on its dog and a lighter one on each favourite that fills it; the fill adds payout, not safety or value.

The market chances here take the margin off in proportion. Taking it equally off each outcome instead (Shin's reading for a fight's or a game's two sides; for soccer's three outcomes the equal margin - Shin's three-way reading needs the draw's price, which the dog files do not keep), the 3,316 UFC dogs priced 2.00-4.00 average a chance of 0.363 against 0.368 and return -5.6% at their price against -4.0%; the 2,157 NFL dogs 0.364 against 0.368, -4.3% against -3.0%; the 8,628 soccer dogs 0.296 against 0.298, -5.3% against -4.7% - so the proportional reading these files use reads every sport's dogs generously.

NFL underdogs are chosen and priced at the closing moneyline (197 of the live draw's 1,487 dogs): the close knows the day's news, and whether a dog is priced 2.00-4.00 is decided at it; live, both are decided at the consensus price when the ticket is built.
UFC cards of 2025 are priced at their opening lines (no closing line is on file for them): 24 of the live draw's UFC dogs that year, 36 of its 266 UFC dogs in all priced at an opening line.

The live draw is the lottery with the live salt (sameday-dog-v1, its seed); the simulation draws are the same lottery with 1,000 other salts. The live draw drew well: over all days its record is above 992 of the 1,000 simulation draws' on the same games (the first years 948, the last 3 years 977), at prices implying -8.5% against -8.5%. Its past draw is no forecast: the simulation draws averaged -9.9% a ticket (-14.7% to -4.7%), and the prices imply -8.5%.

The 5th-95th percentile across the 1,000 simulation draws (-15.6% to -4.3% a ticket over all days) is how much the draw alone moves the record over the same games; it is not a confidence interval. The interval over days is (-9.9% to +7.0% at the live draw; over the 1,000 simulation draws -9.9% (-14.7% to -4.7%), by the prices -8.5%).

Live, a UFC leg is priced from the card the UFC app carries - the best price across books unless the card carries a median from two books or more - and this history prices each fight at one line per card. A best price pays at least a typical book's, so a live UFC dog's price, and whether it falls in 2.00-4.00, can differ from what this record assumes.

Same days and events as the likeliest ticket: on the 1,132 days both exist, the two cannot both win on 102 (the dog is the other side of one of the likeliest ticket's legs). Held together, 1 unit each, they returned +4.0% a unit at the live draw (-2.5% to +10.7%), -1.9% over the 1,000 simulation draws (-6.7% to +3.2%), and -10.2% by the prices; the underdog ticket minus the likeliest was -4.9% a ticket at the live draw, -16.7% over the draws (-26.4% to -7.2%), and +3.5% by the prices.

Prices are the ones on file when the sports' runners last ran: UFC the best price seen across books, NFL the consensus moneyline, soccer the average posted price. One book may pay less. Check every price before betting; a leg whose game has started is never used.
